title: Kayak beneath the cliffs at Pictured Rocks
description: 60m sandstone cliffs on Lake Superior, streaked blue, orange and green by mineral seepage. The lake is cold enough to be genuinely dangerous.

title: Run down the dune climb at Sleeping Bear
description: A 137m sand bluff above Lake Michigan. Going down takes two minutes; coming back up takes most people close to an hour.

title: Cycle around car-free Mackinac Island
description: Motor vehicles have been banned since 1898, so everything moves by horse, bicycle or foot. The shore road is a flat 13km loop.

title: Portage a canoe through the Boundary Waters
description: More than 1,000 lakes linked by portage trails, with motors banned across most of it. You carry the canoe over your head between the water.

title: Walk into the Apostle Islands ice caves
description: Sea caves hung with icicles, reachable on foot only when the lake freezes solid enough - which has happened just a handful of times this century.

title: Take the architecture cruise on the Chicago River
description: The city rebuilt after the 1871 fire and invented the skyscraper doing it. The river was also reversed in 1900 so it flows away from the lake.

title: See your reflection in Cloud Gate
description: Anish Kapoor's 110-tonne stainless steel bean, welded from 168 plates with every seam polished away.

title: Ride the tram to the top of the Gateway Arch
description: 192m of stainless steel catenary curve, ascended in a tram of tilting five-person pods designed in two weeks in 1960.

title: See the exhibits at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
place: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
description: In Cleveland because a DJ here popularised the term in the early 1950s. I M Pei designed the glass pyramid on the lakefront.

title: Go underground at Mammoth Cave
description: Over 685km mapped and still growing - by a wide margin the longest cave system known anywhere, and more than twice the next longest.

title: Follow the Kentucky Bourbon Trail
description: Around 95% of the world's bourbon is made in Kentucky, ageing in charred new oak in warehouses you can walk through and smell from the road.

title: Watch the synchronous fireflies in the Smokies
description: For about two weeks each June, one firefly species here flashes in unison. Access is by lottery, and it is worth entering.

title: Hear a songwriter round in Nashville
description: Broadway is the loud version; the Bluebird Cafe and the writers' rounds are where the songs actually get made, in rooms of ninety people.

title: Stand in the studio where Elvis recorded at Sun
description: A single small room where Elvis, Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins and Jerry Lee Lewis all recorded. Still a working studio at night.

title: Visit the National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine Motel
description: Built around the balcony where Martin Luther King Jr was killed in 1968. Room 306 is preserved exactly as it was that afternoon.

title: Follow the brass bands down Frenchmen Street
description: Where locals go when tourists go to Bourbon Street - live jazz in a dozen rooms within three blocks, most nights of the year.

title: Take a boat into the Atchafalaya swamp
description: The largest wetland and swamp in the US - bald cypress hung with Spanish moss, alligators, and a way of life built entirely on the water.

title: Walk the squares of Savannah
description: Laid out in 1733 around 24 public squares, 22 of which survive, under live oaks hung with Spanish moss.

title: See the wild horses on Cumberland Island
description: A barrier island reachable only by ferry, with feral horses on the dunes and the ruins of a Carnegie mansion in the maritime forest.

title: Paddle the mangroves in the Everglades
description: A river 100km wide and 15cm deep, and the only place where alligators and crocodiles share territory. Go in the dry season for the wildlife.

title: Drive the Overseas Highway to Key West
description: 180km over 42 bridges to the southernmost point in the continental US, built on the piers of Flagler's railway destroyed by a hurricane in 1935.

title: Snorkel the fort moat at Dry Tortugas
description: 113km west of Key West by ferry or seaplane - a vast unfinished brick fort on a sand key, with coral growing along the moat wall.

title: Watch a rocket launch from the Space Coast
description: Launch cadence is now high enough that a week here will usually catch one. The Saturn V hanging in the visitor complex is a real one.

title: Snorkel with manatees at Crystal River
description: The only place in the US where supervised in-water encounters with manatees are legal - they gather in the 22C springs when the gulf turns cold.

title: Walk the Battery in Charleston
description: Antebellum houses along the seawall, and the harbour where the Civil War began at Fort Sumter in 1861.

title: Drive the Blue Ridge Parkway in autumn
description: 755km of ridge road with no commercial traffic and a 72km/h limit. The colour moves down the mountain about 30m a day through October.

title: Climb the Cape Hatteras lighthouse
description: 257 steps up the tallest brick lighthouse in the US, on a barrier island so mobile the whole structure was moved 880m inland in 1999.

title: Walk the catwalk under the New River Gorge Bridge
description: A 24-inch catwalk 260m above the river, under the bridge deck. One day each October it is legal to BASE jump off the top.

title: Drive Skyline Drive through Shenandoah
description: 170km along the Blue Ridge crest with 75 overlooks. One of the few national parks where dogs are allowed on almost every trail.

title: Watch the pony swim at Chincoteague
description: Feral ponies swim the channel between islands each July, herded by the volunteer fire brigade who have run it since 1925.

title: Spend a day in the Smithsonian museums
description: Nineteen museums, all free, including Air and Space and the National Museum of African American History and Culture - the last needs timed passes.

title: Walk the memorials on the National Mall after dark
description: Lincoln, Vietnam and Korea are all open 24 hours and lit at night, when they are far quieter and considerably more affecting.

title: See the cherry blossom at the Tidal Basin
description: 3,000 trees given by Tokyo in 1912. Peak bloom lasts a few days and the date is forecast each year - it has been trending earlier for decades.

title: Tour Fallingwater
description: Frank Lloyd Wright cantilevered a house directly over a waterfall in 1935. Tours must be booked and sell out weeks ahead in autumn.

title: See the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall
description: Both the Declaration and the Constitution were debated in the same room. Free timed tickets, and the queue moves faster than it looks.

title: Walk Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg
description: Crossing the mile of open field the Confederate infantry walked into artillery fire in 1863 tells you more than any museum can.

title: Walk the High Line end to end
description: A disused elevated freight line turned 2.3km linear park through Manhattan's west side. Free, and dogs are not permitted.

title: Cross the Brooklyn Bridge on foot at dawn
description: The first steel-wire suspension bridge, opened 1883. Walk Brooklyn to Manhattan at first light and you will have the promenade to yourself.

title: Spend an afternoon in the Met
description: Two million works across 5,000 years, including an entire Egyptian temple moved stone by stone. Pick two wings and accept you will miss the rest.

title: Eat your way through a New York deli
description: Pastrami cured for weeks and steamed for hours, in rooms that have not been redecorated since the 1950s and are better for it.

title: Count the waterfalls at Watkins Glen
description: Nineteen waterfalls in three kilometres, on a stone path cut into the gorge that goes behind, under and over the water.

title: See all three falls at Letchworth
description: Called the Grand Canyon of the East - a 27km gorge with 180m walls and three major waterfalls, and hot air balloons over it in autumn.

title: Walk the Freedom Trail in Boston
description: 4km of red brick line through sixteen sites, from Boston Common to the Bunker Hill Monument, taking in most of the American Revolution.

title: Cycle the Cape Cod Rail Trail
description: 40km of flat former railway through pitch pine and cranberry bog, with the Atlantic dunes of the National Seashore at the far end.

title: See the first sunrise in the US from Cadillac Mountain
description: From October to March this is the first place in the continental US to catch the sun. Acadia is unusually dog-friendly for a national park.

title: Climb the iron rungs of the Beehive Trail
description: Iron rungs and narrow ledges bolted to a granite cliff, climbed in one direction only. Short, and not for anyone uneasy about exposure.

title: Eat a lobster roll on a working wharf
description: Maine lands most of the country's lobster. The argument over warm butter versus cold mayonnaise is genuine and locals hold firm views.

title: Drive the Kancamagus Highway in October
description: 55km through the White Mountain National Forest with no petrol, no shops and no phone signal - just sugar maples doing their thing.

title: Ride the cog railway up Mount Washington
description: The world's first mountain-climbing cog railway, running since 1869, up a summit that held the world land wind speed record at 372km/h for sixty years.

title: Chase the autumn colour through Vermont
description: Sugar maples turn earliest and brightest here, and the state runs a foliage tracker because the peak moves south about 50km a week.

title: Walk the Newport Cliff Walk past the mansions
description: 5.6km between Gilded Age summer houses and the Atlantic, with public access preserved by colonial-era shoreline rights the owners have fought for a century.

title: Cross the Edmund Pettus Bridge at Selma
description: Where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday in 1965, an event that moved the Voting Rights Act through Congress within months.

title: Drive the Natchez Trace Parkway
description: 715km following a path used for thousands of years, with no commercial traffic and sections of the original sunken trace you can walk.

title: Dig for diamonds at Crater of Diamonds
description: The only diamond-bearing site in the world open to the public where you keep what you find. Several hundred are found each year, most of them small.
